flags.current: A board is allocating capital across two departments, Consumer Credit Cards and Consumer Purchase Loans, whose returns are negatively correlated. Stand-alone 99% VaR is USD 90 million ... USD 110 million ... the combined risk capital requirement is USD 150 million.
flags.proposed: Replace "whose returns are negatively correlated" with "whose returns are imperfectly (less than perfectly) correlated". Answer key (b) is unchanged. Also consider changing Q24's matching stem if it is used as a paired twin; Q24 gives no numbers, so it is not inconsistent on its own.
flags.source_says: The source M2 (page 29) has the same wording and numbers and keys (b). Its 'Source note' (page 30) says the item was rebuilt with 'internally consistent numbers' because the original correlation of -0.7762 did not reproduce the options.
flags.derivation: For two positions, combined capital = sqrt(90^2 + 110^2 + 2*rho*90*110). The zero-correlation value is sqrt(90^2+110^2) = 142.1. A combined figure of 150 > 142.1 implies rho = (150^2 - 90^2 - 110^2)/(2*90*110) = +0.116, a positive correlation. Negatively correlated returns would give combined capital below 142.1 (for example, rho = -0.8 gives 66.0). So the stem contradicts itself. It also contradicts the rule the bank teaches in OR-T1-23: an aggregate above the zero-correlation floor implies POSITIVE correlation. The pro rata arithmetic (67.5 / 82.5) and the key (b) are still right.
flags.evidence: PDF pp.29-30, M2: 'whose returns are negatively correlated ... combined risk capital requirement is USD 150 million'. Compare Q23 solution, p.24: 'An aggregate above the zero-correlation floor implies POSITIVE correlation.'

flags.current: Both were given the following parameters, all expressed as percentages of the loan amount unless stated: ... | Return on economic capital | 0.5% |
flags.proposed: Change the lead-in to "all expressed as percentages of the loan amount except the return on economic capital, which is the rate earned on the economic capital" (or change the table row to "Return on economic capital | 0.5% of economic capital"). Answer key (a) is unchanged.
flags.source_says: The source (pp.13-14) has the same stem wording. Its solution applies 0.5% to the economic capital: 0.005 x 40 = 0.2.
flags.derivation: The solution's claim that the finance department 'reproduces the quoted figures to the basis point' holds only if 0.5% is a rate on economic capital: (7 - 2.5 + 0.2) x 0.7 / 40 = 8.225%, and (7 - 3 - 5 + 0.2) x 0.7 / 40 = -1.40%. The stem literally says every percentage is on the loan amount unless stated, and this row is not flagged as an exception. Read that way, the return on economic capital is 0.5 per 100 of loan. The projections then become (7 - 2.5 + 0.5) x 0.7 / 40 = 8.75% and (7 - 3 - 5 + 0.5) x 0.7 / 40 = -0.875%, and neither matches the quoted 8.23% / -1.40%. A careful candidate who follows the stem literally cannot reproduce the figures that the solution treats as decisive. OR-T1-20 explicitly carves out the return on economic capital; this item does not.
flags.evidence: PDF p.13, Q13 table lead-in: 'all expressed as percentages of the loan amount unless stated'. PDF p.13-14 solution: 'the return on economic capital is 0.5% of that: 0.005 x 40 = 0.2'.
